name: Physical Review B
source: Figure and file-format instructions for authors from the Physical Review B guide 'Documentation_instructions_Physical_Reviews_B.docx'.
rules: Make figures one column wide (8.5 cm or 3 3/8 in), or 1.5 or 2 columns for detailed figures, and make sure everything can be read at that size.
Make the smallest capital letters and numerals at least 2 mm tall.
Make each data point at least 1 mm across, and avoid small open symbols, shading and cross-hatching.
Make curves at least 0.18 mm (0.5 pt) thick.
Label each axis with the quantity plotted and put the units in parentheses after it, not in square brackets.
Use the Greek letter itself (θ), not its spelled-out name (\theta).
Explain the figure's symbols and curves in a legend inside the figure or in the caption.
Label subfigures (a), (b), etc., describe each panel in the caption, and submit multi-panel figures as one file if possible.
Give each figure a single caption that clearly summarizes it, and number figures with arabic numerals in the order the text refers to them.
Use accessible color palettes, with colors that stay distinct in grayscale and different line styles that are described in the caption.
Preferred file formats are .ps, .eps, .jpg and .png, and color-online-only figures must be supplied as .ps or .eps.
Submit photos as high-resolution .jpg or .png files, and if scans can't be avoided, scan at 600 dpi or higher before scaling to final size.
Show the results accurately and state any image changes, such as brightness, in the caption.
